title: Getting started with SITSAR
text: entropy_map() estimates model moving window centred pixel returns map Shannon entropies. Gamma Wishart maps fully vectorised:
code: Hw <- entropy_map(img, model = "wishart", window = 7, L = 4) plot_map(Hw, main = "Wishart entropy (L = 4)") Hhv <- entropy_map(img, model = "gamma", window = 7, channels = "HV") plot_map(Hhv, main = "Gamma entropy, HV (L estimated)")

text: Entropies asymptotically Gaussian, entropy map segmented Gaussian mixture fitted EM (stochastic EM):
code: set.seed(4) seg <- EntropySegmenter$new(k = 3, method = "em")$fit(Hw) seg #> <EntropySegmenter> k = 3 | method: EM  #>   iterations: 20 | converged: TRUE  #>   weights: 0.265 0.268 0.467  #>   class sizes: 5933 5773 10794 plot_map(seg$label_map(), main = "Segmentation (Wishart entropy)",          palette = c("#1f78b4", "#33a02c", "#e31a1c")) kappa_statistics(SanFrancisco150_gt, seg$label_map(), match = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   kappa   variance std_error overall_accuracy     n #>   <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>            <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 0.914 0.00000566   0.00238            0.945 22500

title: Getting started with SITSAR
text: entropy_test() compares two samples entropies: change_map() applies test pixel pixel two co-registered images:
code: set.seed(5) entropy_test(rg0i(300, -3, 2, 4), rg0i(300, -1.5, 1, 4), model = "g0i", L = 4) #>  #>  Shannon entropy test (G0I model) #>  #> data:  rg0i(300, -3, 2, 4) and rg0i(300, -1.5, 1, 4) #> S = 39.345, df = 1, p-value = 3.552e-10 #> alternative hypothesis: true difference in entropies is not equal to 0 #> sample estimates: #> entropy of x entropy of y  #>    0.7615233    1.4698632 set.seed(6) a <- matrix(rgammasar(60 * 60, mu = 1, L = 4), 60) b <- matrix(rgammasar(60 * 60, mu = 1, L = 4), 60) b[21:40, 21:45] <- rgammasar(500, mu = 3, L = 4) cd <- change_map(a, b, model = "gamma", window = 5, L = 4, level = 0.01) cd #> <Entropy-based change map> model: gamma | level: 0.01  #>   size: 60 x 60  #>   changed pixels: 690 (19.17%) plot_map(cd$change, main = "Detected changes") truth <- matrix(FALSE, 60, 60); truth[21:40, 21:45] <- TRUE change_detection_metrics(truth, cd$change) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>      DR    FA    FP    FN    OA #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1   100  6.13  5.28     0  94.7

title: Divergence-based classification with tidymodels
text: sar_features() computes local statistics used engines: Gaussian features (mean_*, cov_*) complex Wishart features (c11, c12_re, c12_im, …).
code: img <- SARImage$new(SanFrancisco150, looks = 4) feats <- sar_features(img, window = 5) feats$class <- factor(as.vector(SanFrancisco150_gt),                       labels = c("ocean", "vegetation", "urban")) dim(feats) #> [1] 22500    21  set.seed(123) split <- initial_split(feats, prop = 0.02, strata = class) train <- training(split) test <- testing(split) nrow(train) #> [1] 448

title: Divergence-based classification with tidymodels
code: spec <- divergence_classifier(divergence = "renyi", order = 0.5, kind = 3) |>   set_engine("wishart") spec #> Divergence Classifier Model Specification (classification) #>  #> Main Arguments: #>   divergence = renyi #>   order = 0.5 #>   kind = 3 #>  #> Computational engine: wishart  rec <- recipe(class ~ ., data = train) |>   update_role(row, col, new_role = "id")  wf <- workflow(rec, spec) fitted <- fit(wf, data = train) pred <- augment(fitted, test) accuracy(pred, truth = class, estimate = .pred_class) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   .metric  .estimator .estimate #>   <chr>    <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 accuracy multiclass     0.932 conf_mat(pred, truth = class, estimate = .pred_class) #>             Truth #> Prediction   ocean vegetation urban #>   ocean       5802         88     0 #>   vegetation     7       6207  1385 #>   urban          0         10  8553

title: Divergence-based classification with tidymodels
code: spec_tune <- divergence_classifier(divergence = "renyi", order = tune()) |>   set_engine("wishart") set.seed(1) folds <- vfold_cv(train, v = 3, strata = class) res <- tune_grid(workflow(rec, spec_tune), resamples = folds,                  grid = data.frame(order = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)),                  metrics = metric_set(accuracy, kap)) collect_metrics(res) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   order .metric  .estimator  mean     n std_err .config         #>   <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>           #> 1   0.1 accuracy multiclass 0.866     3 0.0182  pre0_mod1_post0 #> 2   0.1 kap      multiclass 0.798     3 0.0268  pre0_mod1_post0 #> 3   0.5 accuracy multiclass 0.926     3 0.00815 pre0_mod2_post0 #> 4   0.5 kap      multiclass 0.888     3 0.0123  pre0_mod2_post0 #> 5   0.9 accuracy multiclass 0.969     3 0.00427 pre0_mod3_post0 #> 6   0.9 kap      multiclass 0.952     3 0.00643 pre0_mod3_post0 best <- select_best(res, metric = "accuracy") best #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   order .config         #>   <dbl> <chr>           #> 1   0.9 pre0_mod3_post0

title: Compound complex Wishart models (R6) — CompoundWishart
text: R6 class compound truncated Poisson (CTPCW) compound geometric (CGCW) complex Wishart laws Ferreira, Nascimento Frery (2022); see dctpcw(). title: Divergence-based classifier for SAR/PolSAR features (R6) — DivergenceClassifier
text: Implements family divergence-based classifiers Ferreira, Coelho Nascimento (2021). pixel represented model fitted observations moving window (see sar_features()) class model fitted training pixels. pixel assigned class minimises chosen divergence two fitted models: $$\hat\imath = \arg\min_{\\{1, \ldots, g\}} d(\hat\theta_h,   \hat\theta_i).$$ Two families features available: "gaussian" multivariate normal laws intensity vector, using columns mean_* cov_* sar_features(). class covariance combines average local covariance covariance local means (law total variance). "wishart" scaled complex Wishart laws full PolSAR covariance matrix, using columns c11, c12_re, c12_im, ... sar_features(). Since laws share number looks, rescales divergences affect classification. classifier also available 'parsnip' model divergence_classifier(), use 'tidymodels' workflows.

title: Divergences between Gaussian and complex Wishart models — divergences
text: Available measures (type): "kl" Kullback-Leibler divergence \(D_{KL}(\theta_1 \| \theta_2)\). "jeffreys" Jeffreys divergence \(D_{KL}(\theta_1 \| \theta_2) + D_{KL}(\theta_2 \| \theta_1)\). "bhattacharyya" Bhattacharyya distance \(-\log \int \sqrt{f_1 f_2}\). "renyi" Rényi divergence order \(\alpha\) (order), one four forms (kind): 1, \(D^\alpha_R(\theta_1\|\theta_2)\); 2, \(D^\alpha_R(\theta_2\|\theta_1)\); 3, symmetrised mean \([D^\alpha_R(\theta_1\|\theta_2) + D^\alpha_R(\theta_2\|\theta_1)]/2\); 4, \(c \log\{[K(\theta_1\|\theta_2) + K(\theta_2\|\theta_1)]/2\}\), \(K(\theta_1\|\theta_2) = \int f_1^\alpha f_2^{1-\alpha}\). Gaussian laws Rényi divergence uses normalisation Pardo (2006), \(c = 1/[\alpha(\alpha - 1)]\), gives $$D^\alpha_R = \frac{1}{2}\Delta^\top M^{-1}\Delta -   \frac{1}{2\alpha(\alpha-1)}\log\frac{|M|}{|\Sigma_1|^{1-\alpha}   |\Sigma_2|^{\alpha}},$$ \(\Delta = \mu_1 - \mu_2\) \(M = \alpha\Sigma_2 + (1-\alpha)\Sigma_1\). Wishart laws normalisation Frery, Nascimento Cintra (2014), \(c = 1/(\alpha - 1)\), used: $$D^\alpha_R = \frac{L}{\alpha - 1}\log\frac{|(\alpha\Sigma_1^{-1} +   (1-\alpha)\Sigma_2^{-1})^{-1}|}{|\Sigma_1|^\alpha|\Sigma_2|^{1-\alpha}}.$$ converge Kullback-Leibler divergence \(\alpha \1\).

title: Shannon entropies of SAR and PolSAR models — entropy
text: Gamma \(H = L - \log L + \log\mu + \log\Gamma(L) +     (1 - L)\psi^{(0)}(L)\). G0I (Ferreira Nascimento, 2020) \(H = -\log\frac{L^L\Gamma(L-\alpha)}{\Gamma(-\alpha)\gamma^\alpha     \Gamma(L)} + (1 - L)[\psi^{(0)}(L) - \log L + \log\gamma -     \psi^{(0)}(-\alpha)] + (L - \alpha)[\psi^{(0)}(L - \alpha) +     \log\gamma - \psi^{(0)}(-\alpha)]\). Generalized Gamma \(H = -\log\alpha + \log\Gamma(\phi) + \phi     - (\phi - 1/\alpha)\psi^{(0)}(\phi) - \log\mu\). Scaled complex Wishart (Nascimento, Ferreira Frery, 2023) \(H = m\log|\Sigma| - m^2\log L + \log\Gamma_m(L) + mL +     (m - L)\psi^{(0)}_m(L)\), \(\psi^{(0)}_m(L) = \sum_{=0}^{m-1}\psi^{(0)}(L - )\). G0 polarimetric (Nascimento, Ferreira Frery, 2023) obtained \(E\log|Z| = m[\log(-\alpha-1) - \psi^{(0)}(-\alpha)] +     \log|\Sigma| - m\log L + \psi^{(0)}_m(L)\) \(E\log[L\,\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma^{-1}Z) - \alpha - 1] =     \log(-\alpha-1) + \psi^{(0)}(mL - \alpha) - \psi^{(0)}(-\alpha)\).
